items.title: Monohybrid Cross, Its Interpretation and the Testcross

source_refs.note: Interpretation of the monohybrid cross, gene and locus, the law of segregation, the For Information box and the testcross, as printed (PDF 85-86); Figure 18.1 is the original drawing.

blocks.text: From his experiments, Mendel concluded that for each pair of alternative traits, one trait was not expressed in the F1 hybrids, although it reappeared in 1/4 of F2 seeds. The trait that “disappeared” must therefore be disguised in the F1 seeds.

blocks.alt: A flow from top to bottom. A homozygous round seed (RR) and a homozygous wrinkled seed (rr) each grow into a pea plant; the round-seed plant has its stamens removed and pollen is carried to it from the other plant. Gamete formation gives a female gamete R and a male gamete r, which join at fertilization to give heterozygous round F1 seeds (Rr). An F1 plant grows, self-pollinates and forms female gametes R, r and male gametes R, r; lines join them into F2 seeds RR, Rr, Rr and rr.
blocks.caption: Figure 18.1: Mendel's monohybrid cross (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 18.1).
